findings.issue: ActivateAsync has no rollback after WriteKeyFile. The new AlreadyActivated guard (round-1 finding 1) is `File.Exists(InstallationKeyPath) || File.Exists(DbPath)`, while LoginService.IsActivated is `key file AND db`. If anything fails between WriteKeyFile and a fully seeded database — the disk fills while SeedAsync/StoreAttachmentsAsync writes (exactly the DiskFull result that invites a retry), the schema migration throws, the db file is locked — the key file (and the SQLite file DbSession.Open just created) stay on disk. From then on the machine is permanently stuck: W02/W03/W04 refuse to activate (AlreadyActivated returns «مفعّل مسبقًا» before writing anything), and W05 cannot sign in either, because OpenSessionAsync throws «The database carries no installation identity» and is reported as DatabaseUnreadable. There is no path out of this state from inside the product.
findings.fix: Make activation atomic. Record whether the key file and the database file existed before (AlreadyActivated already guarantees neither did), and in a catch around the whole body — before returning DiskFull/Failed or rethrowing — delete the key file it wrote (and its .tmp/.bak siblings) and the database file it created, restoring the untouched pre-activation state, then return the result. Add a walkthrough test that makes SeedAsync fail (e.g. a read-only data folder or a pre-created unusable wakeel.db) and asserts that after the refusal keys/installation.key is gone and a second, successful ActivateAsync works.

findings.issue: RecoverAsync commits keyFile.Save (new password wrap, new machine wrap and, when issueNewSheet is set, the replacement recovery wrap) BEFORE it opens the database (line 214 vs line 237). If DbSession.Open or OpenSessionAsync then fails with SqliteException/IOException/InvalidOperationException (a db file held open by a second instance or a scanner is the realistic case), the method returns RecoveryOutcome.DatabaseUnreadable with «تعذّر...» while on disk the recovery has in fact happened: the forgotten password's wrap is gone, the new password is already the only one that works, and — worse — the replacement recovery code was written into the recovery wrap and then discarded with the failed result, so it is never shown or printed. The old sheet no longer opens the installation and the new code does not exist anywhere: the account loses its recovery path while being told nothing changed.
findings.fix: Reorder so nothing is persisted until the installation is proven openable: open DbSession with the recovered dbKey first, and only then build the new wraps and call keyFile.Save (still before OpenSessionAsync's writes, but after the connection succeeded); on any failure return without having saved. Alternatively keep the order but, when Save has already succeeded, report success with the new sheet plus the separate warning, never a failure. Add a walkthrough test that makes the database unopenable at that moment (for example by holding the file) and asserts either that the key file is byte-identical to before or that the returned result carries the new sheet.

findings.issue: _lockedOut is derived from _result, and Login.LockedUntil() is only read once in OnInitialized. Once a lock-out has been reported, the «دخول» button stays Disabled for the rest of the session even after the lock-out has expired — typing in the field re-renders but never re-evaluates the lock. The person has to close and reopen الوكيل to sign in after waiting exactly as the screen told them to.
findings.fix: Re-evaluate the standing lock-out instead of caching the result: in OnPasswordChanged (and on a short timer, or on the next SignInAsync attempt) clear _result when Login.LockedUntil() is null, so the button re-enables the moment the wait is over.

findings.issue: In UnlockAsync the finally (lines 192-199) zeroes dbKey and the password-derived vaultKey, but machineDbKey and machineVaultKey are never zeroed when _session.Unlock throws — on that failure path two plaintext keys are left in managed memory, which is the exact leak the round-1 finding 9 fix closed everywhere else.
findings.fix: In the catch for the Unlock failure, zero machineDbKey and machineVaultKey (when they are not the same arrays as dbKey/vaultKey) before returning DatabaseUnreadable.

findings.issue: VerifyAsync returns immediately when _verifying is set and schedules nothing afterwards. A keystroke that lands while the (deliberately slow) Argon2 verification of the previous text is running is dropped for good, so a complete, correct code can leave step one un-green and SubmitAsync refuses it with «الرمز غير مكتمل» until the person edits the field again.
findings.fix: Remember the text that arrived while a verification was in flight and re-run VerifyAsync once the running one finishes (a simple pending-text field plus a loop), so the last text typed is always the one that gets a verdict.

findings.issue: FailedAttempts/LockedUntil/LockRounds live only in keys/session.dat, which is sealed with machine-scope DPAPI inside a folder the host deliberately grants BUILTIN\Users Modify on. Any local account can delete the file to reset the attempt counter and the temporary lock-out to zero between rounds, so the W05/W06 lock-out is a UI delay rather than a limit. (Offline attack on installation.key is anyway the dominant threat, which is why this is low rather than higher.)
findings.fix: At minimum treat a missing card on an activated machine as suspicious — keep a second, coarser counter that is mirrored into the account row and re-applied on the next successful open — or state in the package notes that the lock-out is a convenience limit only, so nobody later relies on it as a security control.

findings.issue: Recovery code attempts are not counted at all: Verify (called from W07 on every keystroke) and RecoverAsync go straight to the key wrap with no reference to LoginService.LockOutInForce/RecordWrongPassword, so the recovery dialog is the one place in the product where secrets may be tried without limit. The code's entropy makes this cheap to live with, but it is inconsistent with the lock-out the same key file enforces for passwords.
findings.fix: Route a CodeWrong outcome through LoginService.RecordWrongPassword (or a separate, looser counter) and refuse Verify/RecoverAsync while LockOutInForce stands, exactly as LockService.UnlockAsync now does.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS RE-CHECKED, ALL GENUINELY FIXED: (1) ActivateAsync refuses before WriteKeyFile via AlreadyActivated and returns ActivationResult; W02/W03/W04 each carry the `if (Login.IsActivated) -> /login` guard — but the fix introduced the medium finding above (no rollback, AlreadyActivated using OR while IsActivated uses AND). TESTS ARE REAL, NOT TAUTOLOGIES: the walkthrough drives the whole path on a temp root and asserts database rows (4 org_units, 1 device, role Secretary, 4 documents, the four settings keys), files on disk, all four wrap kinds in the key file, audit entries for sign_in / sign_in_failed / lock / unlock / recover, the old password dying after recovery, and a byte sweep of every written file plus the log for the passwords, the package password and both recovery codes in UTF-8, UTF-16 and base64. Refusal states (wrong package password, foreign organisation, other machine, older sequence, future date) each assert IsAcceptable false, no key file, and an Arabic-only, jargon-free message. 52 bUnit facts cover all six screens and their states, including the tooltip-on-every-icon-button check and the bidi isolates.

ARABIC / RTL: every user-facing string in Ar.FirstRun.cs is Arabic; the only Latin tokens are the ones the owner allows (the file extension, QR, PDF, USB, Ctrl+P, Caps Lock, Enter) and the risky ones carry explicit U+2066/U+2069 isolates inside the constant (the extension with its leading dot, the Caps Lock key name); numbers and mixed lines go through <Bdi>/<bdi>. The first-run and sign-in routes use BareLayout — no sidebar — and the approved brand.

BUILDER'S OWN OPEN ISSUES — I agree with all three: the WPF drop cannot be synthesised over CDP (the WebView swallows drops over the content area anyway, so the window-level handler is the right belt-and-braces and is covered at the unit level); the disk-full state cannot be staged in the suite; and ARCHITECTURE.md §3's machine-scope DPAPI MachineWrap with constant entropy is implemented exactly as the document mandates (I read §3 line 62 to confirm) — that is a specification question for the owner, not a defect in this package.

VERDICT: fix — two medium findings (activation has no rollback and can brick the machine; recovery persists the new wraps before proving the database opens and can destroy an unseen replacement recovery code). Neither is reachable on the happy path, which is why the suite is green; both are small, local changes plus one test each.
